question: A shopkeeper marks the price of an article at ₹1,980. Find the cost price if after allowing a discount of 12% he still gains 32% on the cost price.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct ratio: CP / MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%)

⇒ CP / 1980 = (100 − 12) / (100 + 32)

⇒ CP / 1980 = 88 / 132

⇒ CP / 1980 = 2 / 3

⇒ CP = 1980 × (2 / 3) = 660 × 2 = 1320

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,320.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹1,980

Discount = 12%

Profit = 32%

**Formula:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − Discount%)/100

Cost Price (CP) = SP × 100/(100 + Profit%)

 
• CP SP MP 
 +32% Profit 
 −12% Discount MP = ₹1,980 CP = ? 
 

**Step 1: Calculate Selling Price (SP)**

⇒ SP = 1,980 × (100 − 12) / 100

⇒ SP = 1,980 × 88 / 100

⇒ SP = 1,980 × 0.88 = ₹1,742.40

**Step 2: Calculate Cost Price (CP)**

⇒ CP = 1,742.40 × 100 / (100 + 32)

⇒ CP = 1,742.40 × 100 / 132

⇒ CP = 174,240 / 132

⇒ CP = ₹1,320

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,320.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relation between CP and MP

CP / MP = (100 − D%) / (100 + P%). This is the fastest way to solve questions involving both discount and profit.

Marked Price (MP)

MP = CP + Markup. Markup % = (Markup / CP) × 100. It is the price listed on the tag before discounts.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts d₁% and d₂% are given, total discount = [d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂)/100]%.
